summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of liver transplant presented with a two-day history of fever and transient confusion, peaking at 102°F. He denied respiratory, urinary, or gastrointestinal symptoms but noted increasing bilateral leg edema. Transferred from an outside hospital after initial evaluation suggesting possible pneumonia, he was admitted for fever monitoring and infectious workup. Chest X-ray and abdominal ultrasound showed no acute abnormalities, including no signs of infection, ascites, or liver dysfunction. Laboratory studies revealed stable liver function, normal white blood cell count, and renal function within his baseline range. Sirolimus level was therapeutic at 7.4. He remained afebrile during admission, with no evidence of bacterial infection. Blood and urine cultures were pending at discharge. The fever was attributed to a likely viral illness. No medication changes were made. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all home medications and follow up with the liver transplant clinic.
